questions.answer: Read the durable result with task_status or wait for it. A wait timeout leaves the child running; known child work must finish before result_available.

questions.answer: T3-owned delegation can choose a different compatible provider instance/model rather than only a native harness child.

questions.answer: T3 MCP and V2 child-thread lifecycle own delegation and durable results; this is distinct from provider-native subagents.

questions.question: Followup
questions.answer: Send to childThreadId to continue its conversation. After the original task completes, a follow-up becomes a fresh task without rewriting the published result.

questions.answer: The model calls delegate_task with a prompt, optional role and target. task_status, task_cancel and wait inspect or control the execution.

questions.question: Schedules
questions.answer: Tasks support recurring intervals or fixed times and a one-time date and time, on the selected environment server.

questions.question: Events
questions.answer: Webhook tasks accept external requests with optional signatures, filters and deduplication. PR watchers also wake agents on changed checks, comments or conflicts.

questions.question: Recurring tasks
questions.answer: Scheduled prompts can post into an existing thread or start a fresh thread per run. Users can edit, pause, resume or delete schedules.

questions.question: Completion conditions
questions.answer: Delegated task results wait for known child work to finish. A scheduled dispatch is not documented as acceptance of the requested business outcome.

questions.question: Scheduler location
questions.answer: The chosen environment owns app scheduler execution even without an active turn. Fixed-time recurrence uses its time zone.

questions.question: Overlaps
questions.answer: Webhook keys suppress duplicate requests for seven days; coalescing combines a burst into its latest payload and survives restart. General limits on overlapping recurring runs remain unestablished.

questions.question: Retries
questions.answer: One-time runs missed while offline execute when the environment returns. Webhook senders normally redeliver errors; optional T3 Connect buffering lasts up to 24 hours and can skip old requests.

questions.question: Client independence
questions.answer: The background service runs as a service for the user on Linux and macOS; on Linux lingering keeps it running after logout, while macOS stops it at logout and Windows has no background service. Process independence, not an unattended trigger.

sources.finding: Threads with optional New worktree, project-less threads, background starts, multi-model send via Shift-click, pin/settle/snooze, Working section (beta), automatic settlement, and an Agents view for work delegated to subagents. Thread order is saved on the server.

sources.title: Messages and context (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Attach files, Send while the agent is working, Custom models, Edit an earlier prompt, Commands and skills, Context in your message
sources.finding: Attachments (up to 100 files), queued or steered follow-ups, custom model IDs, edit-and-rewind from an earlier prompt, slash commands and $ skills, review-comment and pull-request context chips, mobile offline queueing.

sources.title: Running T3 Code in the background (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Manage the service, Platform support
sources.finding: Background service on Linux (systemd user service with lingering) and macOS (launch agent while logged in); Windows background services are not supported.

sources.title: Codex provider (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Connect with ChatGPT, Use multiple accounts
sources.finding: Connects with a ChatGPT plan or an existing Codex CLI login; multiple accounts selectable from the model picker; usage and credits managed in ChatGPT.

sources.title: Claude provider (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Separate accounts or configurations, Skills, OpenRouter
sources.finding: Uses Claude Code's own login and configuration; separate accounts through CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR instances; skills from the config directory and .claude/skills; OpenRouter or router setups through instance environment variables.

sources.title: Antigravity provider (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Models and threads, Skills and attachments, Subagents
sources.finding: Pinned v0.1.7 Antigravity guide: lists images, PDFs, text and audio as native attachments; plan mode unavailable; skill directories and subagent batching. Main-branch attachment narrowing is in docs-antigravity-main.

sources.title: Mobile notifications (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: whole page
sources.finding: Mobile alerts when an agent finishes, fails, needs approval or asks for input; background delivery requires T3 Connect and a direct or Tailscale connection alone does not enable push.

sources.title: Welcome wizard (v0.0.45)
sources.locator: Connect your computers, Check your agents, Import your projects
sources.finding: First-run flow connects computers, checks Claude Code and Codex install/sign-in, and best-effort imports recent Claude Code and Codex projects and conversations.

sources.title: T3 Code releases
sources.locator: release list
sources.finding: Current release list includes v0.1.8 nightlies. GitHub latest resolves to stable v0.1.7, displayed November 4. Old v0.0.45 is historical, not latest.

sources.title: T3 Code Security Policy
sources.locator: Document dates: effective and last updated November 6, 2026; Reporting security issues
sources.finding: Policy effective and last updated November 6, 2026, reread November 7. The vendor aims to acknowledge complete security reports within one business day. This is a reporting target, not general support response or an independent assurance certificate.

sources.title: T3 Code Terms of Service
sources.locator: fees, accounts, availability, warranty sections
sources.finding: Terms effective July 15 still state no T3 Tools subscription fee unless a feature states otherwise; third-party costs remain user responsibility; account-backed services and early-stage availability differ. Future paid features show prices before purchase.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7 outside agents
sources.locator: MCP URL; sign-in modes; host scripts; revocation
sources.finding: Remote HTTP MCP with OAuth exposes project/thread read, start, message and stop operations. Read-only is default; granted modes cap spawned/steered thread permission. Host t3 thread start/send/show/list uses the same tools. Credentials last 30 days and can be revoked. These are threads, not documented native issues.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7
sources.locator: Latest stable; release timestamp; tag resolved with git ls-remote
sources.finding: Latest stable resolves to v0.1.7 displayed November 4. Tag points to commit 322f6544dfad0a3c8a0c8cbecf2c7f7874b14268.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/faq.md
sources.locator: Cost; local models; remote; subscription usage
sources.finding: FAQ explicitly rejects local model support, describes currently free T3 Code and three free T3 Connect machines, and separates provider charges. Code and prompts go from the user host to the provider; Connect sets up a tunnel. Subscription compliance statements are vendor claims.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/providers-acp.md
sources.locator: Local commands; registry; credentials; permissions; checkpoints
sources.finding: Local commands and registry agents run on the environment host and retain native tools, login and settings. Models and features depend on advertised capabilities. T3 provides its own MCP scheduling and delegation, while native sandbox and rewind behavior vary.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/outside-agents.md
sources.locator: Read-only default; approved scopes; host scripts; revoke
sources.finding: OAuth HTTP MCP supports project and thread read/start/send/stop and provider discovery. Read-only is default; approved modes cap operations. Login requires HTTPS or localhost; sign-ins last 30 days and can be revoked. Host CLI scripts can return thread IDs, replies and outcome codes.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/permission-modes.md
sources.locator: Initial default; child requests; provider differences
sources.finding: New threads initially use Full access, with user and project overrides. Supervised asks for command and edit approval, Auto-accept edits covers edits, and Auto uses a provider reviewer where available. Child approvals appear in the parent; provider enforcement differs.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/project-settings.md
sources.locator: Scheduled tasks; Webhooks; scopes and cleanup
sources.finding: Environment-owned tasks support once, recurrence and webhooks. Webhooks offer signatures, filters, seven-day dedupe and restart-persistent coalescing. Optional Connect buffering holds offline requests for up to 24 hours; cleanup controls are separate and default off.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: apps/web/src/components/chat/ProposedPlanCard.tsx
sources.locator: Plan actions: copy, download Markdown, save workspace; TimelineAssistantRows integration
sources.finding: The rendered plan card exposes Markdown, copy, download and workspace save guarded by filesystem-write permission. The thread timeline renders these artifacts. This does not establish a maintained spec or approval workflow.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md
sources.locator: Purpose; provider injection; delegate_task; task_status; follow-ups; scheduled tasks
sources.finding: T3 MCP delegates child threads across compatible providers with roles, models, scoped credentials, idempotency keys and durable task results. Children receive the supplied task and optional role without parent history. Follow-ups preserve the published result and run as a fresh task.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/orchestrator/tools.ts
sources.locator: OrchestratorToolkit; delegate_task/task_status/schedule_task; McpHttpServer registration
sources.finding: The stable OrchestratorToolkit registers delegation, status, cancellation, thread and schedule tools, and McpHttpServer registers that toolkit. Tool descriptions expose isolated worktrees and model/role choices, connecting the contract to the shipped path.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/thread-sidebar.md
sources.locator: Inspect agent work; Resume at reset; side chats; thread metadata
sources.finding: Threads support manual Resume and optional reset-time continuation. Parent conversations show child questions and approvals. Side chats can bring context back; saved thread metadata and message search are documented.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/providers-pi.md
sources.locator: Permission modes; extensions; durable delegation
sources.finding: Pi approval modes apply through a blocking tool hook, explicitly not an OS sandbox. Trusted extension code retains the Pi trust boundary. T3 delegate_task creates durable child threads distinct from an installed native subagent extension.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/portable-handoffs.md
sources.locator: Context selection; omitted history retrieval; limits
sources.finding: Portable handoff selects bounded original and recent messages and results, excluding reasoning, tool state and attachments. References allow retrieving omitted saved history. A full window can start a fresh provider conversation; the new request is never shortened.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/thread-migration.md
sources.locator: Migration; Continuing; recovery copy
sources.finding: V1 migration copies SQLite and imports messages, attachments and settings but not the old live process, run/checkpoint, approval or plan state. Continuation starts a fresh provider session with bounded history. No whole-thread export command exists; a stopped userdata backup is the documented recovery path.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/providers-opencode.md
sources.locator: Local/external server; approvals; refresh
sources.finding: After lost connection, another prompt reconnects to the same OpenCode session. Restricted modes require approval for environment files. Allow for workspace affects matching requests across sessions; denial does not end the whole turn.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/terminal.md
sources.locator: Terminal history limits
sources.finding: The environment server retains at most 5,000 lines and 8 MiB of terminal scrollback, dropping oldest output at either limit. Reconnect and restored history share those bounds; retained output can be copied.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/telemetry.md
sources.locator: Product events; mobile crash report; own OTLP receiver
sources.finding: Server product events exclude prompts, responses, files and authentication data. Mobile crash reports can include handled error values and have an opt-out. Operators can export traces, metrics and logs to their own OTLP receivers; server telemetry and managed-policy controls remain separate.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/guest-links.md
sources.locator: Beta setup; Send/Dismiss; What the guest sees; attachments
sources.finding: Optional beta links require Labs and T3 Connect, authorize one browser for 24 hours and stream recent/live thread history. Guest text and files wait for the owner to Send or Dismiss. Guests lack model, file, rewind and provider-answer authority; ending sharing revokes access.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/managed-policy.md
sources.locator: OS rollout; enforcement; capability/provider permission caps
sources.finding: Administrators deploy JSON, macOS device profiles or Windows Group Policy. The server enforces locked settings and limits for all clients, rejects invalid policies and reloads only on restart. This is machine management, not organization SSO or SCIM.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/source-control.md
sources.locator: PR review and mobile; Review guides; viewed marks; watchers; stacks
sources.finding: Stable mobile PR review supports diffs and draft comments. Optional beta guides tour every changed file, group mechanical changes and hide stale excerpts. Server-retained viewed marks show Changed after pushes. Shared PR polling wakes agents for checks, reviews and conflicts; GitHub stack actions are available.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: remote access
sources.locator: T3 Connect, scripts, LAN pairing and remote machines
sources.finding: Agents execute on a user-owned machine running the environment; clients connect over T3 Connect, private pairing or SSH. The host must remain running and reachable. A separate remote host continues work when the laptop client disconnects.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/background-service.md
sources.locator: Manage the service; Platform support; Troubleshooting
sources.finding: On Linux and macOS t3 service install runs T3 Code as a per-user service. Linux setup enables lingering so it keeps running after logout; the macOS service stops at logout; Windows background services are not supported.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/keybindings.md
sources.locator: Composer controls; Copy pull request references; Find in a diff; Commands with special behavior
sources.finding: Shortcuts are customised in Settings > Keybindings on web and desktop. thread.stop interrupts the running turn and has no default shortcut. mod+f searches a Diff panel or pull request Code tab diff (not configurable); mod+shift+c and mod+shift+k copy a PR URL or number.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/mobile-notifications.md
sources.locator: whole page
sources.finding: With T3 Connect and Device Notifications enabled, phones get alerts when an agent finishes, fails, needs approval or asks for input. Background delivery requires T3 Connect; the app need not keep a connection to the environment.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/user/updating.md
sources.locator: Before you update
sources.finding: Server updates can interrupt active agents and terminal commands; saved threads, settings and project files remain. Settings > Maintenance > Continue threads after restarts is on by default and resumes supported active threads after an update, crash or machine restart; threads without saved provider resume state need a new message, and after three automatic resumes in a row a thread waits for the user.

sources.title: T3 Code v0.1.7: docs/internals/overview.md
sources.locator: Turn completion and checkpoints
sources.finding: Checkpoints use hidden Git refs to capture workspace state without adding commits to the user's branch. A provider that cannot roll back its conversation must reject a revert before the filesystem changes.

sources.title: T3 Code remote access guide
sources.locator: remote-access.md at 9cd7a04: introduction, T3 Connect, SSH and Load balancing sections
sources.finding: Agents run on a machine you control that must stay running and reachable; clients connect over T3 Connect, direct pairing or SSH, and several machines can be load balanced. Changes since 322f654 are wording and CLI-command edits; no T3-operated compute is described.

sources.title: T3 Code provider execution boundary
sources.locator: docs/user/providers-acp.md local commands and permissions; apps/server/src/provider adapter spawn paths and managed worktree setup
sources.finding: T3 Code launches installed coding-agent/ACP processes on the environment host and separates optional worktrees. Native ACP/provider policies own process sandboxing. The scoped core has no product container or per-agent VM provisioning backend.

sources.title: T3 Code persistent workflow inventory
sources.locator: Migrations.ts and persistence/Migrations/OrchestrationV2; contracts and thread sidebar searched for issue, backlog, task state and scheduled task
sources.finding: The persisted workflow model contains projects, threads, provider sessions, reviews and scheduled-automation definitions/history. It has no separate native issue/backlog entity with an issue state lifecycle. Settled/archived threads and scheduled automation settings are not independent native issues.

sources.title: T3 Code environment access model
sources.locator: EnvironmentAuthPolicy.ts descriptor; auth/PairingGrantStore.ts, SessionStore.ts and RpcAuthorization.ts; managed-policy guide
sources.finding: The environment authenticates paired devices using bootstrap credentials, cookies, bearer/DPoP access tokens and scoped grants. Machine management policy is separate. The scoped core has no named organization/project human membership roles or enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO integration.

sources.title: T3 Code user-owned provider keys
sources.locator: Claude provider guide OpenRouter configuration; Fees in official T3 Code terms; README sales FAQ
sources.finding: Provider instances can configure the user's OpenRouter API key through ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN. The README says T3 Code is not selling an app plan, and current terms impose no T3 Tools subscription fee while assigning provider and host charges to the user.
